--- original

@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 8d80
+title: 'mlx: cache the generated custom-kernel source and library name per call site (upstream patch)'
+---
+## Why
+^xdrv99b profiled Inkling decode, which makes ~430 custom-kernel calls per token. For every call, mlx (mlx-swift 0.33.0):
+- `fast::metal_kernel`'s closure runs `write_signature`, which builds header + source + signature into a new string, several KB per call.
+- `CustomKernel::eval_gpu` computes `std::hash<std::string>{}(source_)` over that whole string, then `fmt::format`s the library name, on every encode.
+
+Together they take ~15–20% of the decode main thread, and every model with custom kernels pays them.
+
+## What
+- In the `metal_kernel` closure, memoize `kernel_name` and `kernel_source` by the template args and the input/output dtype signature. A small map in the closure, behind a mutex.
+- In `CustomKernel`, compute `lib_name` once at construction.
+- Measure with a locally patched mlx-swift checkout: `swift package edit`, or a path override in inklingcli.
+- Write up the result and a draft upstream PR for the user. Do not open the PR.
+
+## Acceptance
+- [ ] inklingbench.sh with the patched mlx shows the decode gain.
+- [ ] The diff and the PR description are drafted for the user to review. #inkling-perf
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    ## Result: a small gain, not worth an upstream patch on its own (patch kept: scratchpad/mlx_kernel_cache.patch)
+    - Patch, applied with `swift package edit mlx-swift` in inklingcli: the `metal_kernel` closure memoizes the generated source per kernel_name, and `CustomKernel::eval_gpu` memoizes the lib_name per (name, compile options, source length).
+    - Profile: `mlx_fast_metal_kernel_apply` falls from 11.9% to 9.3% of the main thread, and `CustomKernel::eval_gpu` from 19.4% to 18.5%. The source copy into each new CustomKernel, the make_shared and the Swift wrapper (`MLXFastKernel.callAsFunction`, ~12%: Zip2Sequence, utf8CString, dynamic casts) remain.
+    - inklingbench vs base: decode +1.6% at 2k, +1.4% at 8k, +2.2% at 32k, +3.9% at 64k. Prefill flat. CHECK PASS.
+    - Conclusion: the custom-kernel cost is spread over generic per-op overhead (array allocation, encoder state, Swift bridging), not one string hot spot. The lever is fewer graph nodes per step and less Swift graph building (compile, ^jddp2ck). Not drafting an upstream PR now; the patch is kept for later.
